tasks.details_markdown:
**Interface:** Fresh remote main, the original source manifest, and applicable Accepted
specifications produce an MW-only preflight with exact paths and an authority-by-authority
delta. This is documentation, not a new runtime API.

Pin HEAD and compare with 6f610253. Reread affected memory/retrieval/material/pool/worker/
Console paths. Check tracked names, SQL objects, API inventory, and pending branches for
collisions. The original plan must not claim 0195/14E; supplied archive 0196 is occupied too.
Reconcile all candidate migration names, not only the first occurrence. Record read versus
unavailable sources, scope, and required amendments. Do not alter PLAN.md, P04 preflights,
or frozen specifications just to satisfy a checker.

A01 is an observational preflight, not an artificial RED/GREEN exercise. Preserve unrelated
dirty bytes and review source drift before writing.

**Interface:** Existing toolchain/scripts produce an accurate command/role/development-dependency
matrix. The Cargo reference is E01; browser infrastructure belongs to T03.3.

Check the configured disposable PostgreSQL namespace and restricted runtime login. Record
which suites actually execute without changing old evidence. Verify explicit doctests;
do not invoke an absent general npm test. Read the actual authentication flow and approve
supported labels, ordinary-material reads, and counter boundaries. A missing environment
is BLOCKED, not PASS inherited from another commit. Browser/DB unavailability cannot be
replaced with a test double for qualification.

For A51, only the observed command and exit establish execution. This preflight needs no
artificial business-logic mutation.

**Interface:** Proposed MemoryReadRepository::detail(&RequestContext, MemoryId) returns
Result<Option<MemoryDetail>, ApplicationError>; revision(&RequestContext, MemoryId,
MemoryRevisionId) returns Result<Option<Revision>, ApplicationError>. MemoryReadService
applies existing capability/content/disclosure policy before DTO conversion. Keep application
results separate from HTTP serialization and reuse RequestContext/Memory/MemoryRevision.

Open one consistent scoped read for memory, active revision, and permitted origins. Validate
revision/workspace identity and current content rights. Return only permitted fields;
unknown/denied objects share 404. Wire actual server and MCP composition rather than leaving
an unnoticed default-unavailable adapter. Preserve the old metadata GET. MW-02 supplies
exact new provenance links; legacy associations remain legacy_unattributed.

A02/A09 require real server/MCP composition and refusal without source metadata leakage;
a direct service-object test alone is insufficient.

**Interface:** Proposed MemoryReadRepository::list(&RequestContext, BrowseRequest) returns
MemoryPage; history(&RequestContext, MemoryId, HistoryRequest) returns RevisionPage, both
through Result<_, ApplicationError>. BrowseRequest includes kind/status/collection filters,
limit, and opaque cursor; HistoryRequest includes limit/cursor. Follow chapter 02.6.
The collection filter is unavailable until MW-04 supplies its lawful relationship.

Apply disclosure predicates before keyset (created_at,id) selection with limit N+1. Bind
cursors to scope/filter/epoch/policy without hidden IDs. History filters inaccessible content
and pins the highest visible revision on page one. MW-01 applies M01 schema and transactional
epoch triggers covering existing writers. Test read consistency now rather than defer it to
MW-02; the correction receipt schema exists, but its new writer is enabled in MW-02.

A03/A04 cover equal timestamps, concurrent mutation, explicit cursor expiry, and direct
historical URL authorization. No silently duplicated/omitted records.

**Interface:** Proposed ContextDeliveryService::build(&RequestContext, ContextRequest) returns
Result<ContextResponse, ApplicationError>. QualifiedTextCounter::count(&str) returns
Result<u32, ApplicationError>, with identity() -> &str and registration bound to an approved
model/destination. No default counter promises an arbitrary-model ceiling. Consume existing
RetrievalService/ContextPack items and output the exact sections/rendered_context schema.
Byte-only output is not normative ContextPack2 qualification.

Use existing generation/policy guards and hydrate only authorized exact revisions. Render
real content and retain SourceRef; omit absent text instead of substituting explanation.
Build one deterministic final string with citations/separators and enforce its complete
UTF-8 cap. Qualified token mode counts that final string; missing counters return 422.
Recheck policy/generation before disclosure: one bounded stale retry without a new external
dispatch, otherwise a typed error.

Run A06–A08 and cross-cutting A09/A52. Estimates cannot silently become strict guarantees.

**Interface:** MemoryMutationPlan carries authenticated context, target/base content and state
revisions, action payload, reason, exact source link, and semantic key. Proposed
MemoryMutationRepository::apply_in(&RequestContext, &mut dyn UnitOfWork, &MemoryMutationPlan)
returns Result<MutationReceipt, ApplicationError>. Reuse InstallationMutationPermit and
GovernedMutationRepository::commit_in. Result IDs become authoritative at caller commit;
no child method commits independently. Applied M01 is a dependency, not a writable task file.

Take approved guards and existing database CAS with bounded revision conversion. Write
capture/correction Event, MemoryRevision, MemorySource, exact link, and storage projection
in the same UoW. Shared governed mutation includes audit/outbox/receipt. The database trigger
advances epoch once; do not repeat it in application code. No provider/vault/network work
runs inside the transaction. Do not edit the M01 checksum or infer old attribution.

A05/A10 verify exact new provenance and rollback of revision/audit/outbox/receipt/epoch,
including active-head integrity.

**Interface:** Proposed MemoryMutationRepository::commit(&RequestContext, MemoryMutationPlan)
returns Result<MutationReceipt, ApplicationError>, coordinating the existing UoW and apply_in.
Use chapter 02.5 key scope, normalized input, and approved keyed commitments, not generated
result IDs. Store the receipt schema without plaintext bodies.

Reauthorize and lock the existing canonical key. Exact committed replay returns the original
receipt before stale CAS and never invokes Apply again. Changed intent returns 409; pending
contenders wait boundedly or receive busy. Only the no-receipt path applies and commits.
Replay lost responses from durable state. Exercise independent connections and actual child
process death after commit/before response. Removing the winner check must fail the unchanged test.

A11–A13 require one effect, identical winner receipt, changed-body refusal, and no receipt
access for an unauthorized principal.

**Interface:** POST corrections accepts closed CorrectionRequest with a required UUID key,
returning 201 MutationReceipt. action=restore reads old content under current policy and
creates a new revision. Preserve legacy remember/revise signatures and MemoryResponse;
adapt both to the shared participant. Inherit labels, without a new classification write field.

Validate closed bodies. Preserve legacy numeric If-Match; new corrections use explicit body
preconditions only. Refuse restore when target classification would weaken source obligations.
Execute the common writer with 409 on basis mismatch. Do not infer extra lifecycle actions.
Update route inventory, schema generator, and production composition together. Replay precedes
CAS through the same writer. Run legacy regressions alongside the new endpoint suite.

A14–A16 require concurrent-edit protection, restored text in a new r5 with history preserved,
and no remaining legacy non-atomic bypass.

**Interface:** Proposed MemoryClient methods list(BrowseRequest), detail(memoryId),
history(memoryId,cursor), correct(memoryId,CorrectionRequest,key), and context(ContextRequest)
follow the schema. Existing transport owns authentication and error parsing. Mount real
/memory routes with browse/detail/history states. Create test:memory before its first invocation;
T03.3 adds browser testing.

Reuse transport without adding browser token storage. Map closed DTOs and abort requests on
scope change. Distinguish browse/search, empty/503, and safe 404/403 responses. Use existing
design primitives without hardcoded successful mock data. Compare actual served JSON.

Create tsconfig.memory-tests.json and scripts/run-memory-tests.mjs in the approved package.json
scope. Compile pure editor/client helpers without React DOM to an isolated temporary output,
run named node --test targets, remove output, and preserve nonzero compile/test exits.
Do not assume unsupported native Node TypeScript behavior. This pure runner adds no production
dependency. A17 must preserve request_id and show unavailable rather than an empty library.

**Interface:** Proposed EditorState variants are viewing, editing(base,draft),
submitting(base,draft,key,request), conflict(base,current,draft),
result_unknown(base,draft,key,request), and failed(base,draft,error).
reduceEditor(state,event) is pure; drafts stay in browser memory, not persistent cache.

Save captures the exact body and UUID key once; retry reuses both. A 409 preserves base,
current, and draft. Only explicit user acceptance of a new basis creates new intent/key.
Timeout becomes result_unknown, not a claim of no change. Restore requires a reason.
Logout/workspace switch cancels pending requests and clears plaintext state. Treat can_correct
as a hint subject to server checks; show classification read-only with an explanation.

A18/A19 verify stable retry identity, preserved unresolved drafts, and discarded late
responses from the previous scope.

**Interface:** Reuse test:memory and introduce test:e2e:memory. Choose and lock an exact
Playwright development-only version during dependency review. Do not claim a browser is
installed without verifying it. Real E2E targets a prepared HTTP server and creates data
through production endpoints. Keep credentials out of test source, screenshots, and reports.

Reuse T03.1's pure-TypeScript runner; add browser infrastructure/fixtures here. Bootstrap
only the installation, then invoke real POST operations. Test keyboard editor/restore,
two-user CAS, unavailable state, hostile text, and late scope-switch responses. Sanitize
output. A mock server does not qualify the backend; typecheck is not browser execution.

A20/A21 require no script/remote-image execution, accessible focus/error/status behavior,
and recorded actual browser results.

**Interface:** Proposed SourceCollection/KnowledgeSource/SourceRevision/SourceImportOperation/
SourceImportItem follow chapter 02. Use existing typed-ID macros. SourceImportRepository
provides create_collection(ctx,CreateCollectionRequest,key), get_operation(ctx,id), and
closed-schema source listing/history. M02 creates MemorySourceBinding with manual_override=false,
exact origins, and item receipts; MW-05 adds resolution rather than inventing binding later.

Create scoped keys/FKs and immutable revisions with ordinary-material references. Identity
is collection + external UUID, not global hash. Through the shared writer record capture
Event, one Observation memory, and exact revision link. Do not auto-confirm facts or elevate
labels. Check supported policy and exact catalog/grant names on clean and populated databases.

A22/A23 plus A28 require distinct source identities, immutable payloads, and no authority
from imported instructions.

**Interface:** Proposed SourcePayloadStore::stage(ctx,operation_id,item_id,bytes) returns
StagedPayloadRef; read(ctx,ref) returns a protected bounded buffer; retire(ctx,ref) returns
a lawful erasure outcome. References carry same-workspace ordinary material/intent identities
and readiness evidence, never arbitrary paths. SourceImportService::preview(ctx,request,key)
returns 201 only for a fully durable ImportPreview.

Bound/validate input, reserve operation/items and ordinary intents, then commit intent before
vault work. Prepare ciphertext outside SQL through the existing protocol. Recheck item bindings
and publish immutable PreviewReady only after all inputs are durable. Pre-preparation death
means needs_upload; retransmission retires the old reservation lawfully before a successor.
Never guess plaintext or trust client-fabricated hashes/receipts. Exact body/key returns the
winner; changed body returns 409. Read policy precedes source content disclosure.

A24/A25 verify exact staged bytes, both preparation/crash boundaries, and no plaintext fallback.

**Interface:** Proposed local CLI:
`vestrace sources scan --root <explicit-root> --state-file <outside-root> --output <sealed-input>`.
Preview/apply/status use HTTP. ScannerManifest matches SourceDocument; keep UUID mappings
outside the input root. Input shape follows ImportPreviewRequest with .md/.txt or closed JSON.
The server accepts no source path/URL to read itself.

Open the explicit root and reject nonregular/symlink/reparse or ambiguous hard-link scope
according to the supported platform policy. Capture bytes once, validate UTF-8/BOM/limits,
and retain stable mapped IDs; do not reread at Apply. Reject absolute/dot-dot/drive/backslash
ambiguity and path collisions. Uncertain rename requires user mapping, not inode/time/hash guesses.
The server repeats decoded-size and duplicate-key checks. A complete scan must actually cover
its scope; interruption means partial with no Missing assertion.

A26/A27 cover Windows junctions/Linux symlinks/traversal and byte-versus-character limits.
Record tested platforms and refuse unsupported safe modes.

**Interface:** SourceImportApplyHandler implements existing OutboxHandler with topic
memory.source_import.apply. handle(ctx,message) reads durable operation/item authority,
not a client-supplied principal. SourceImportService::apply(ctx,id,ApplyImportRequest,key)
returns ImportOperation. A separately checked cancel command is completed in MW-05.
The handler participates in MemoryMutationRepository::apply_in and uses item receipts.

Lock collection/operation; check exact preview, selection, expiry, and current rights.
Atomically transition/enqueue through the registered topic, processing bounded items.
Each item reauthorizes the original actor, checks immutable inputs/base versions, and commits
source/memory/audit/outbox/receipt together. Business outcome is durable before the dispatcher's
separate acknowledgement. Replay converges. Show application separately from index_state;
unavailable embeddings do not erase pending obligations. Complete from durable results,
including partial failures, not unconditional success.

Run all A28–A31, including revoked-actor handling. Real worker --once and process-death replay
are required, not only direct service calls.

**Interface:** Trusted internal SyncFacts compares immutable B/I/M payloads, identities, and
override state; it cannot be deserialized from HTTP. classify_sync returns the closed decisions
Unchanged/Rename/Update/Conflict/Missing/Blocked. Read materials under authorization, compute
equality outside SQL, then recheck exact versions under locks. No public digest oracle.

Identical identity/content with no relevant change is Unchanged. Locator-only change with
established identity is Rename, not a content revision. I != B without an edit allows Update;
manual override or changed M requires Conflict. Partial scans cannot assert Missing; complete
scans may record it, not deletion. Changed labels are Blocked. Existing open conflicts produce
conflict_pending, not an overwrite. Enumerate decisions and reject client comparison flags.

A32/A36 verify no extra canonical revision for unchanged/rename and no purge from Missing.

**Interface:** SourceSyncService::resolve(ctx,conflict_id,ResolveConflictRequest,key) returns
MutationReceipt. Only accept_source/keep_manual/merge are accepted with common idempotency
and exact conflict/memory/incoming-source preconditions. One source has one open conflict.
ConflictDetail exposes immutable original_manual_revision=M0 and permitted current
manual_revision=M separately; current need not equal detection-time M0.

Take approved collection/source/conflict/memory guards and reauthorize every basis. Check
current pointer/state and immutable conflict refs without silent rebase. accept_source creates
I and clears override; keep_manual preserves M and its revision with a recorded override;
merge creates explicit user text with override. Atomically record resolution Event, binding,
version, audit, and receipt before closing the conflict. Source bytes never change.

Show M0→M, retain drafts after stale rejection, and refresh bases. Ordinary correction updates
manual_override in the shared MW-02 writer files; include both in exact scope before editing.
A35 must first reject stale resolution, then succeed after fresh detail while preserving M0
and the intervening edit. No model-driven merging.

**Interface:** cancel(ctx,operation_id,CancelRequest,key) returns ImportOperation.
collection.active_import_id serializes batch admission, not ordinary editing. Item/completion
locks fence post-cancel writes. Cleanup consumes existing retention/material authorities,
not an independent scheduler.

Reject a second active Apply while permitting individual edits. Before item commit, recheck
bases and cancellation under consistent lock order. A committed-first item stays committed;
cancellation skips the rest. A winning cancel prevents later mutation. Expiry applies to
staging/preview_ready; accepted Apply owns its material until lawful retirement. Clear the
active import only after a durable terminal outcome. Replay cancel from its receipt; elapsed
time does not prove a writer dead.

A37–A39 exercise both winners with bounded race/crash fixtures. No fictional rollback or
erasure of already applied material is acceptable.

**Interface:** MemoryExportService::prepare(ctx,ExportRequest,key) returns ExportOperation.
MemoryExportHandler uses existing OutboxDispatcher/topic memory.export.prepare.
download(ctx,id) returns bounded JSON/Markdown only after current read/export authorization.
Persist selection/result refs and serialize only the PortablePackage allowlist.

Select a bounded permitted immutable revision set and safe provenance closure. Atomically
record operation, selection, audit/outbox; render via ordinary materials outside SQL.
Publish Ready only for the exact complete protected result. Reauthorize every pinned source/
memory/revision at download; any revoked access blocks the entire output and initiates lawful
retirement. Use existing expiry; no public/CDN/static URL bypass.

A40/A41 require exact selected scope, no authority fields, and refusal after revocation even
when preparation succeeded earlier.

**Interface:** validate_portable(bytes:&[u8]) validates the closed versioned PortablePackage,
limits, and references. PortableImportMapping is operation-scoped foreign-to-local mapping,
not imported trust. Reuse mode=portable and the same handler's persisted phases entities →
links → complete; do not add an unhandled topic.

Before mutation validate version, depth, bytes, nodes, intra-package refs, and active revision
selection. Allocate mappings once per operation. Import each entity/history with actual
importer and local recording time; keep origin actor/time as annotations. Local policy owns
classification; reject imported grants/confirmed flags and never copy ACLs. The same topic's
idempotent linking pass reuses mappings after entity commits. Keep partial until closure.
Exact replay reuses IDs; new explicit imports warn about duplicates rather than overwrite.

Run A42–A45 including linking restart and authority rejection, not only parser success.

**Interface:** CLI sources export submits ExportRequest, polls ExportOperation, and downloads
through existing HTTP transport. UI selection/history/format/reason is explicit and displays
status/expiry. Markdown is a deterministic reading representation, not a backup format.

Create a stable key once per intention and poll boundedly without new operations. Download
only by explicit user action; no embedded tokens or plaintext content cache. CLI writes only
to a selected safe destination, refuses overwrite by default, and tests platform permissions.
Escape Markdown delimiters and mark partial history/provenance and origin annotations.
Warn that client copies cannot be revoked by the server and transfer no authority.

A46 and the download flow verify exact selection, escaping, explicit rather than automatic
export, and truthful expiry.

**Interface:** Consume logical M01–M04, existing provisioner/schema gates, and ordinary-material
requirements. Produce restricted-runtime clean-install/upgrade/refusal observations—not a
new repair authority.

Prepare a disposable clean database and a populated baseline via real old interfaces. Apply
forward migrations and exact roles; compare historical data and legacy receipts. Attempt
raw DML on every new guarded table and cross-workspace reference and assert the intended
refusal mechanism. Test ordinary-material recovery/erasure with source/export refs and no
cross-source cascade leakage. Existing migration checksums and protocol locks remain unchanged
outside approved new scope.

A47/A48 require both clean and populated upgrade under the limited runtime role. A privileged
fixture cannot replace those checks or conceal missing grants.

**Interface:** Consume actual built binary, HTTP, worker, Console, registered topics, scoped
fixtures, and the complete A01–A54 matrix. Produce a versioned evidence manifest with source,
build, environment, exact commands, and limitations. MW completion does not set TRUSTED.

Run upload → read → edit → sync conflict → resolve → export → new target with production
producers. Kill actual child processes after business commit/before acknowledgement and
during linking; inspect durable outcomes through a fresh reader. Compare served OpenAPI,
actual JSON, and SDK fields. Run doctests and browser checks explicitly. Mutate receipt/CAS/
workspace/atomicity/override/download-policy guards in disposable copies, restore, and rerun.
Independent final review reads the whole contract and current tree; list unresolved material,
generation, migration, or environment blockers. Qualify only the approved supported scenario,
not full v1.0 or P04 closure.

Run all linked A49/A50/A52/A53/A54 and complete relevant suites. Syntax/typecheck alone is
never feature acceptance.
